newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Nordbanken denies in deal with S-E-Banken.
newsitem.headline: Nordbanken denies in deal with S-E-Banken.

text.p: State-contolled Swedish bank Nordbanken on Sunday denied a report that it was selling its international division and mutual funds operation to rival commercial bank S-E-Banken.

A report in Swedish business daily Dagens Industri a day earlier said Nordbanken was close to reaching a comprehensive cooperation agreement with S-E-Banken in which it would take over S-E-Banken's nationwide network of bank offices.
The report, citing unnamed sources, also said S-E-Banken would buy the Nordbanken operations and become a merchant bank.

"Nordbanken continues to be open to discussions about various types of mergers, with S-E-Banken and other banks, on the condition that it results in a long-term increase in value for Nordbanken's shareholders," Nordbanken said in a statement.

"In such a deal, it would not be possible for Nordbanken to transfer control of business divisions or operations such as its international ones or mutual funds which belong to its core activities," the bank said.
"Nordbanken aims to develop its service and product line to private customers as well as companies and institutions," the bank said, adding that would not comment further on the speculation.

"The banking market has, for a while, attracted structural changes. Nordbanken has expressed interest in taking part in these changes and from time to time has participated in exploratory discussions," Nordbanken also said.
Swedish banking shares have risen sharply since last autumn on rumours of a shake-up in the sector, widely seen to be over-supplied and ripe for mergers.
